articles.head: 'Social contagion': where the idea came from
body: The idea that teenagers 'catch' being trans from their friends goes back to one study.

readings.label: One reading
readings.text: A 2018 study asked parents about their teenagers. It said some came out suddenly, inside friendship groups, and called it 'rapid-onset'.

readings.label: Another reading
readings.text: In March 2019 the journal corrected it: 'rapid-onset' is not a formal diagnosis, and the study heard only from parents, not the young people or their doctors.

articles.source: Source: Littman, PLOS ONE, 2018, and the journal's correction, 19 Mar 2019.
summary: A 2018 study of parents' reports named 'rapid-onset'.
A 2019 correction says it is not a formal diagnosis.

articles.head: US report: 'talk therapy first'
body: A US health department review, 1 May 2025, after the executive order 'Protecting Children From Chemical and Surgical Mutilation'.

readings.label: The report
readings.text: The evidence for medical treatment in young people is low quality. Talk therapy should come first, including 'exploratory therapy'. Calling that conversion therapy is 'misguided'.

readings.label: Its critics
readings.text: The American Academy of Pediatrics and others say it breaks with the major medical bodies, hides its authors, and its 'exploratory therapy' can include conversion practices.

articles.source: Source: US Department of Health and Human Services, review of 1 May 2025, and KFF's explainer.
articles.mumNote: even the government says talk first, love

articlesRetired.head: More than one in eight 'went back', study finds
body: A US survey asked 27,715 trans adults about their lives.

readings.label: The headline
readings.text: Of those who had transitioned, 13.1% said they had detransitioned at some point.

readings.label: The reason
readings.text: 82.5% of them named at least one pressure from outside. The most common: pressure from a parent.

articlesRetired.source: Source: Turban et al., LGBT Health, 1 Jun 2021 (the 2015 US Transgender Survey).

articlesRetired.head: More than one in eight 'went back', study finds
body: A US survey asked 27,715 trans adults about their lives. Of those who had transitioned, 13.1% said they had detransitioned at some point.
Most named pressure from outside: 82.5% cited at least one external factor, led by pressure from family and stigma.
articlesRetired.source: Source: Turban et al., LGBT Health, 1 Jun 2021 (the 2015 US Transgender Survey).

articlesRetired.head: Why people stop: pressure from family tops the list
body: 82.5% of those who had detransitioned named at least one outside reason. The most common: pressure from a parent (35.6%).

clip._docS360: ⚑ S360 (his 11 Nov: 'Is it the AI that makes the video of the social contagion to her?' — yes; and 'music and a narrator'): the clip is no longer a recommended video from a channel ('Concerned Futures · 1.2M views' is gone). Second Thoughts MAKES it for Maya out of her own week — the lot's five (Ola, Priya, Rae, Sam, Maya), her 18th, the clinic number 4,815, Meridian's no — in the genre's overblown, glossy voice (his rule for the system's new media), and the last frame turns the genre's alarm into the system's promise. `channel`/`recommended` keep their old keys only because browser.ts still prints them: `channel` is now the stamp line 'Made with AI', `recommended` is 'made for you'. NEVER a medical or diagnostic word in a frame; never a joke at Maya. THE NARRATOR is the SYSTEM's synthetic voice (apparatus register): one build-time TTS file per frame, tools/tts/render.py, entries clip_narr_0…6 in data/audio/tts_manifest.json, whose `source.fields` are `clip.frames[n]` below so the spoken words cannot drift from the subtitles. `frameHolds[n]` = that file's real duration (ffprobe: 3.692 2.438 3.622 3.204 3.762 3.831 3.065 s) + the narrator's 0.15 s entry + at least 0.6 s of air, rounded up to a half-second so every card starts on a beat of the music (120 BPM): 4.5 4 4.5 4 5 5 5 = 32 s; `frameSeconds` is kept as the fallback for a caller with no holds. The music (clip_music.mp3, tools/make_clip_music.py) is one loop of the same length. ⚑ S364: ten frames now, 50 s — the numbers here are S360's; `_docS364` has the current ones.
clip._docS364: ⚑ S364 (UiB job 14 Part B item 3 / N8; his verdict on the 32 s cut, 11 Nov: 'looking super good… needs a bit more of content, maybe we can push to 45 seconds? the music was great, and the voice it made was brilliant'). THREE CARDS INSERTED after '18 TODAY' (frames 3–5): THE SIGNS — the parent-reported 'signs' the 2018 paper lists (RESEARCH_ROGD_AND_FILTERS_2026-11-11 §B1: a sudden announcement, friends who also came out, more time online, popularity after coming out, earlier struggles) turned into the AI's CHECKLIST APPLIED TO HER WEEK, over the top: a panel titled THE SIGNS whose rows accumulate (card 3 rows 1–2, card 4 rows 1–4, card 5 all five, then a 5 / 5 stamp), each tick landing on a beat as the narrator finishes its sentence (`signs.cards[].ticks`, seconds into the card). THE COLLAPSE IS BUILT IN: every tick carries its 'evidence' from her own data in small mono type, and the evidence does not support it — 'came out suddenly' is proved by Mum's line from June 2023 (her own years thread: 'so proud of you love'), three years before this week; 'friends came out too' by the size of her group chat; 'more popular after' by the stream that comes for her later. The clip never names the theory and never says it is real; the correction stays readable in Mum's article; no medical or diagnostic word on a card ('struggles', not a condition). Frames 6–9 are S360's frames 3–6, unchanged, and their narrator files were RENAMED clip_narr_3…6 → clip_narr_6…9 (his 'brilliant' takes kept, not re-rendered); clip_narr_3…5 are new, same manifest voice and settings (M5, speed 0.85, 12 steps). `frameHolds[n]` = the file's real duration (ffprobe: 3.692 2.438 3.622 4.110 4.807 5.782 3.204 3.762 3.831 3.065 s) + 0.15 s entry + at least 0.6 s of air, rounded up to a half-second: 4.5 4 4.5 5 6 7 4 5 5 5 = 50 s = 25 bars at 120 BPM. ⚑ He asked for about 45: the narrator's own pace on the three new lines (two sentences each) needs 18 s by the rule; S360's holds were kept so every later card keeps its place in the bar (the only shorter honest total, 48.5 s, would take S360's spare half-second off card 1 and its spare second off the last card, and leave the loop half a bar short). The music (tools/make_clip_music.py) is the same piece, longer: 25 bars, the later cards moved by exactly 9 bars, a ding on every tick and a stamp-hit on 5 / 5.
